title: Analyze tier structure
notice: Demo with sample data only. It is not connected to your organization's data, and it should not be.
question: As Loyalty Program Director, review the synthetic tier structure without changing member status.

answer.question: As Loyalty Program Director, review the synthetic tier structure without changing member status.
answer.answer:
Here's the synthetic tier structure review — no member status changed.

**Tier Ladder**
| Tier | Threshold | Multiplier | Added Perk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bronze | $0 | 1.0x | Birthday bonus, member sales |
| Silver | $1,000 | 1.25x | + free standard shipping |
| Gold | $3,000 | 1.5x | + free express shipping |
| Platinum | $6,000 | 2.0x | + personal shopping advisor |

**Sample member progress:**
- Platinum member: $6,200 spend, engagement 92 — top tier achieved
- Gold member: $3,400 spend, engagement 75 — 56.7% to Platinum ($2,600 to go)
- Silver member: $1,600 spend, engagement 58 — 53.3% to Gold ($1,400 to go)
- Bronze member: $450 spend, engagement 32 — 45% to Silver ($550 to go)

Spend gaps roughly double at each tier, which is a healthy progression curve. If you want, I can pull `program_improvements` for ideas on tightening engagement-to-spend correlation or flag where members are stalling.
